reason: PASS through content regexes, a stand-in for a JSDoc parse. One regex per tag family keeps one finding per tag (a comment holds several); named groups anchor on the tag name after the `@` (capture.TAG) and on the `{type}` of `@param`/`@returns` (capture.TYPE). The regexes do not check that the tag is inside a `/** */` comment, so `@param {x}` in a string or line comment would be a false positive; jsdoc-parse is the principled form.

evidence.why: `/** @typedef {number} T */`: capture.TAG starts at 1:6, the tag name, as TSLint
`@param {number} x Is a number`: capture.TYPE starts at 14:11 at `{number}`

audit.note: Content regexes per tag family stand in for a JSDoc parse and are not confined to `/** */` comments: `// @param {string} x` or a string containing `@type {x}` is flagged though TSLint only reads JSDoc.
